01.speaker: narrator
01.text: A road is cut into the wall of the Rift. It took us a day to walk down it. At the bottom we went through the gap in the Black Gate one at a time, the way his armies had come out.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: Behind the Gate is the Hollow, a cavern under the world so big its roof is lost in the dark. The only light is grey fire. A day's march in stood his fortress, Nhal Vorath, built from the ruins of his old city, which sank with him.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: His army was still too big to storm. So we dug in in front of his walls, built our towers, and let it come to us.

04.speaker: vael_orrun
04.text: You built your city on my city, and you lock my door with my own crown. Come in, then.

05.speaker: tamsin
05.text: For once we're not holding a road, Spirewright. We're on his.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Every land we had freed sent its fighters to Solenne: Emberfolk smiths, Galeborn riders, Deepwood archers, Tidefolk, Stoneborn and Veilwalkers.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: Cassivane came for the Heartstone himself. He had fused the pieces of the Sunstone into his own body. We called what he had become the Sundered Heart.

03.speaker: ysolde
03.text: If he takes the Heartstone, the Gate opens all the way and Vael-Orrun walks out. So he does not take it. Hold this wall.

04.speaker: ysolde
04.text: ...There's a light on the east road. Does nobody else see it?

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: With all six Wardens awake, their oath held Vael-Orrun again, and the gap in the Gate could get no wider. Only the whole Heartstone could break the oath now.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: So everything he had left came out of the Rift at once and marched west for Solenne, with Cassivane at its head. We raced it home.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: The Wardens walked with us.

04.speaker: thalassa
04.text: Queen of Solenne. When this is over, I will tell you what we did at Vael. Not before.

05.speaker: narrator
05.text: Cassivane's army was camped at Crossmere, the town where every road on the Ring meets, a day east of Solenne. We had to go through him.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: We held Crossmere. Cassivane fought like the hero he used to be, then pulled back with what was left of his army.

02.speaker: cassivane
02.text: Yes. I opened the Gate. He had my daughter. He gave her back to me empty. She will be whole when he is free.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: He left her behind. In the cage was Ilyra, six years gone. She was alive, but she did not know her own name.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: Corvin sat with her all night. By morning she knew his name. By the next, she knew her own.

05.speaker: ilyra
05.text: Behind the Gate I heard two voices. One of them wept. The other never did. My father only ever heard the first. Let me help you stop him.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: The Sundered Heart had reached the inner wall when a white light came up the east road.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: It was Oswin. He had fallen through the Gate at the start of the war and walked back under the world, through the Hollow, and climbed up out of the Rift. The Unbound would not go near his lantern.

03.speaker: oswin
03.text: Hello, Ysolde. I'm sorry I'm late. I found this at the bottom of the Rift. I think it's yours.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: He climbed the Spire, set the last piece in the Sunstone's frame, and lit it with his lantern. The dark sank back into the Rift, and the sun came up over Solenne for the first time in months.

05.speaker: narrator
05.text: The Unbound around the walls burned in it. Only the Sundered Heart kept coming.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: On the Kharum Terraces Gorrath came down the steps himself. He had gone to the Rift two years ago and come back with his heart cut out and a carved stone in its place. When it cracked, he broke apart into boulders that kept rolling, then stopped.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: Behind a fallen terrace we found what was left of the Canyon's shield-company. Gorrim Stonebeard was standing in front of them, with a stone door for a shield. Twenty years ago he had held the Kharum Pass beside Gorrath.

03.speaker: gorrim
03.text:
One iron ring in my beard for every friend I've buried. He makes thirty-two.

Let's not make it thirty-three.

04.speaker: gorrim
04.text: One iron ring in my beard for every friend I've buried. Thirty-one. Let's not make it thirty-two.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Sunscar Canyon is red rock. The Stoneborn live in cities carved into its walls. Its Warden, Orrok, sleeps in the mountain at its head, under Grundhallow.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: Orrok had gone mad, and the canyon turned on the Stoneborn. Its walls broke off and walked. Every oath carved in its cities broke at once, and the oath-breakers turned to stone and marched. Their Herald was Gorrath, the Stoneborn general who once held the Kharum Pass for a month.

03.speaker: kaela
03.text: Stone doesn't feel a blade. It feels lightning. Give me towers that throw it, and I'll do the rest.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Under Grundhallow the Mountain Titan fell, a giant of grey stone. The grey came off it like dust, and under it was Orrok.

02.speaker: orrok
02.text: ...Thank you.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: It was the first thing he had said in two thousand years. The walking stone lay down, and the Stoneborn buried their dead in the Deep Halls.

04.speaker: gorrim
04.text: That's the last ring. Hear me say it. No more.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: At Brazier Hold Ashwick came down the road himself, running, the way he always ran. He was born in Kethra. As a boy he swept Brannoc's forge; then he became the Concord's youngest messenger. Two years ago he ran east to the Rift, and nobody knew why.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: When he fell, we found Brannoc Emberhand, the smith who forged Solenne's gates, chained in his own forge. Ashwick had kept him there nine days to make him forge chains for the horde.

03.speaker: brannoc
03.text:
Nine days that boy asked me for chains. He used to sweep my floor.

Nine days I told him no. Now give me a wall to stand on.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: The Ember Reach is a land of volcanoes, and the Emberfolk forge in their heat. Its Warden, Ignar, sleeps in the fire under the mountain of Pyrrhenhall.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: Ignar had gone mad, and the mountain's fire came out to burn the people it once kept warm. Out of it walked the Herald's army: cinder hounds, smiths sealed in slag, the smoke of burned houses. At its head ran a boy made of embers, the Herald Ashwick. The town of Kethra was first on their road.

03.speaker: fennick
03.text:
I'm Fennick. I design the towers; you build them. Those things are made of fire, so fire won't hurt them. Water will. And you, child, will place it where I tell you.

Hold the road to Kethra. Ashwick is somewhere up that mountain. Kill him, and his army loses its head.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Under Pyrrhenhall we fought the thing Ignar had become, the Cinder Tyrant, a giant of grey fire. When it fell, the grey burned off it, and Ignar woke.

02.speaker: ignar
02.text:
A boy of my own people sat by my fire and whispered, until I forgot what I was. I burned the people I swore to keep warm.

I am awake now. I will burn for you.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: With its Warden awake, the fire went back under the mountain. By morning the slopes had cooled to black stone, and the Emberfolk lit their forges again.

04.speaker: fennick
04.text: One land back. Five to go. Pack your tools, Spirewright. The Thunder Steppe is next.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: We walked back up the Rift road. When the last of us was through, the six Wardens shut the Black Gate and sealed it with their oath. It has not opened since.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: Every town we had held was still standing, and its people went home.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: We buried Fennick under the east gate he held, and Seraphel beside the Sunstone.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: I am Ysolde, Queen of Solenne. I am old now, and I have never seen a dawn since. But I have felt every one of them.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: When the Sundered Heart broke, Cassivane was inside it, burned grey, holding his locket.

02.speaker: ilyra
02.text: Father. Look at me. I'm whole. I got better on my own. He lied to you.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: He looked at her for a long time. He put the locket in her hand. Then he died.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: I felt the sun on my face. I could not see it, but I felt it. Solenne stood.

05.speaker: oswin
05.text: The Gate is still open a cart's width, and he is still behind it. While it's open, he will keep sending armies through. So we go down there and end it.

06.speaker: narrator
06.text: For the first time in the war, we did not wait for him to come to us. We marched east, to the Rift.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: By then it had been dark for months. Crops failed. Solenne lived by torchlight on rationed bread.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: I ruled by voice. I learned people by their footsteps.

03.speaker: tamsin
03.text: Fennick wrote everything down. Which towers work where, and why. I'll read it to you, Spirewright. Badly.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: The dark came from the Rift, and the further east we went, the thicker it got. East was where we were going.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Prism Wastes is the glass plain in front of Solenne. Cassivane's whole army came across it, and we fell back to the walls.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: That night the Lumen Gate fell, the outer wall of Solenne. It was the only wall we lost in the whole war.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: Behind it, Seraphel drew her sword. She was the last knight of the Sunstone, and its light had kept her alive for a thousand years. Since it broke, she had been dying.

04.speaker: seraphel
04.text: I have a few days left. Let me spend them on your wall.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: At Elderhollow Mother Briar fell, and the thorns that had grown through her went brown and crumbled. For forty years she had healed the Deepwood. Two years ago she went east to the Rift, like Ashwick, like Vholt. Before she died, the grey went out of her eyes.

02.speaker: mother_briar
02.text:
The Marshal sent us to the Rift. Six of us. Study the Gate, he said...

He knew what was behind it.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: Cassivane was my Marshal and my friend. I did not believe her. I thought it was the madness talking.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: In the root-halls we found Sylvaine Thornwhisper, the Deepwood's best archer. She had held the root-doors alone while the whole town climbed out.

05.speaker: sylvaine
05.text: They're all out. Every child. Now show me where to stand.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: The Verdant Deep is a forest of trees as tall as towers. The Deepwood live in the branches. Its Warden, Elowen, sleeps in the oldest tree of all, at Sylvanmere.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: Elowen had gone mad, and her forest turned on the people who lived in it. Thorns closed the roads. Oaks tore up their roots and walked. Leading them was the Herald Mother Briar, the Deepwood's wisest healer, grown through with thorns.

03.speaker: tamsin
03.text: Fennick says green wood rots in the dark of the Rift, so build the void towers. I say build them fast. Those trees are walking toward Fernholt.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: At Sylvanmere we cut Elowen out of the Elder Broodmother, the rotten thing that had grown over her inside the oldest tree. She was very old, and very tired.

02.speaker: elowen
02.text: The tree is dying. It has one seed left. Take it, child, and plant it somewhere the dark can't reach.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: The thorns let go of the roads, and the walking oaks lay down where they stood. Three lands were free, and we went home to Solenne for one night's rest.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: We came home to Solenne for one night. Three lands were free. We thought the worst was over.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: At midnight, the east gate opened from the inside. Our own soldiers opened it. Their eyes were grey and empty.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: Cassivane had been emptying our soldiers for months, the way the Heralds were emptied, and keeping them in the barracks under our own colours. Two thousand of them.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: Fennick held the gatehouse with half-built towers and a hammer.

05.speaker: fennick
05.text: Don't stand there, Spirewright! Get to the palace and get the Queen out. I've got the gate.

06.speaker: narrator
06.text: The gatehouse came down on him. He held the gate until it did.

07.speaker: narrator
07.text: Cassivane climbed the Spire of Aurel to the Sunstone. Its light burned the things of the dark, and he had become one of them. He broke it.

08.speaker: narrator
08.text: Then he came down for the Heartstone, the key to the Black Gate. Six years ago he had chipped a sliver off it, and that sliver opened the Gate. Now he wanted the rest.

09.speaker: narrator
09.text: I got there first. I took the Heartstone and ran. The pieces of the Sunstone were falling all around me, and their light was the last thing I ever saw.

10.speaker: cassivane
10.text: Give me the stone, Ysolde! He has my daughter. He gives her back when the Gate is open!

11.speaker: narrator
11.text: Tamsin got me out. Cassivane gathered up the pieces of the Sunstone and fled east. One piece he never found. It had fallen all the way to the Rift.

12.speaker: narrator
12.text: With the Sunstone broken, nothing held the dark down in the Rift any more. Before morning it came up and spread across the sky. The sun did not rise. That was the start of the Long Night.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Two thousand years ago there were seven kingdoms: six in a ring, each with its own magic, and Orrun in the middle, where all their roads met.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: The songs say Orrun's king, Vael-Orrun, wanted all six crowns. He learned a power that makes magic stop. Where his armies walked, fire would not burn.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: The six monarchs beat him. They drove him and his army down the Rift, a chasm miles deep, and shut them behind the Black Gate at the bottom.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: They made its key from his crown: the Heartstone. Then they gave their lives to keep the Gate shut. Their spirits sleep in their lands. We call them the Wardens.

05.speaker: narrator
05.text: On his ruins we built Solenne, my city, with the Heartstone at its heart and the Sunstone above it, a lens whose light the things of the dark cannot bear. That is how the songs tell it.

06.speaker: narrator
06.text: Six years ago, my Lord Marshal, Cassivane, lost his daughter Ilyra in the Rift.

07.speaker: narrator
07.text: This spring, somebody unlocked the Black Gate. We did not know who.

08.speaker: narrator
08.text: Oswin, the master of our Order, turned the light of all his towers on it and drove it back, until the gap was only as wide as a cart.

09.speaker: narrator
09.text: Then the ground gave way, and he fell through. His lantern was still lit.

10.speaker: narrator
10.text: Six armies came out through the gap, each led by a grey-eyed champion we called a Herald. Each Herald went home, to the land they were born in. A Warden lets its own people come close.

11.speaker: narrator
11.text: There each Herald whispered to its Warden until the Warden went mad. A mad Warden turns its own element on its own people. The volcano poured out its fire. The forest strangled its towns. And the Herald raised an army out of the land itself.

12.speaker: narrator
12.text: I am Ysolde, Queen of Solenne. You are a Spirewright, the last of Oswin's apprentices. You build the towers. We take the lands back one at a time. Hold the road to each town. Kill its Herald. Free its Warden. Hold the road.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: People who fled before we reached their towns came up the roads to Solenne. We gave them the squares, then the gardens, then the halls of my palace.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: The Lord Marshal Cassivane commanded our armies. He met every cart at the gate himself. Six years after he lost his daughter, he still wore her picture in a gold locket.

03.speaker: cassivane
03.text: You are winning, Spirewright. Every life we lose out there will be paid back. I promise you that.

04.speaker: narrator
04.text: Six years before, my half-brother Corvin had called him a traitor. Then Corvin was found over a dead man, and I exiled him. I believed Cassivane.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: The inner wall broke, and Cassivane took the Heartstone. No. That is not how it happened. Again.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Over Highwind, Kaela Stormrider brought Vholt's bird down with her own lance. She was the Galeborn's war-leader, and he had taught her to ride. For eleven days she had fought his army alone, falling back from camp to camp.

02.speaker: vholt
02.text:
Kaela... someone I trusted asked me to go to the Rift. So I went. I'm sorry, girl.

Finish it. Clean, the way I taught you.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: She finished it facing him, the way he taught her.

04.speaker: kaela
04.text: Eleven days I rode away from his army. I hate riding away. Point me at the next one.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: The Thunder Steppe is grassland on a high plateau. The Galeborn live there on horseback and steer by the storms. Its Warden, Aurath, sleeps in the storms themselves.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: Aurath had gone mad, and the storms turned on the camps they used to guide. Lightning struck the tents. Dead riders came back on horses of lightning. Over them, on a bird of black cloud, rode the Herald Vholt Stormcrown, the warchief who had taught half the Steppe to ride.

03.speaker: fennick
03.text:
The Galeborn don't build walls. Your towers are the only walls they've got. And lightning doesn't hurt lightning. Build stone. It grounds the stuff.

Start at Stonering Camp.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Over Aurvanis we brought down the Thunderhead, a storm gone solid as black glass. It was Aurath's madness. It shattered, and for the first time in a month the rain fell with no lightning in it.

02.speaker: aurath
02.text:
A voice I knew told me my riders had betrayed me. So I struck them down, camp by camp.

Never again. My winds are yours.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: The dead riders fell from their horses where they stood. The Galeborn rode home to Aurvanis. Two lands were free.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: When his army was spent, he came out himself.

02.speaker: vael_orrun
02.text: Six of you. Always six. Ask them what they did at my table.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: None of the Wardens answered him.

02.speaker: the_hush
02.text: He was the first to listen. I taught him how a world goes quiet.

03.speaker: the_hush
03.text: Every word he whispered to your Regent, I had whispered to him first.

04.speaker: the_hush
04.text: I could never climb out of the dark. So I waited for you to carry me home.

05.speaker: the_hush
05.text: Your High King was never my enemy. He was my hand. So were you.

07.speaker: the_hush
07.text: Seven crowns. One door. Thank you.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Brannoc broke the outer gate. Seraphel held the inner gate open with her back until the last of us were through. Then her light went out.

02.speaker: seraphel
02.text: Tell Ysolde I saw one more dawn. That was all I wanted.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: We found him in his ruined throne hall, on his knees. The monster's shape was cracking off him, and there was a tired man inside it.

04.speaker: thalassa
04.text: I gave away my forgetting, so I remember everything. You should know what we did.

05.speaker: thalassa
05.text: He kept the peace between us for forty years. We feared him, and we wanted his gold.

06.speaker: narrator
06.text: They came to his feast as friends. At midnight they opened his gates. His city burned, and his wife and son burned with it. The songs call it a victory. The Wardens call it the Night of Six Knives.

08.speaker: vael_orrun
08.text: You did this. Remember that you did this.

10.speaker: vael_orrun
10.text: That night a voice in the dark taught me how to make magic stop. I thought it was my own grief. It was never my own voice. It is still listening.

11.speaker: narrator
11.text: Mirelle had seen a death at the end of the war. It was his.

12.speaker: narrator
12.text: Oswin pressed his lantern into the burning core in his chest. He turned to light, and the light went up out of the Hollow, home to Solenne, into the Heartstone that had been his crown.

13.speaker: narrator
13.text: He wanted the middle of the world. So we gave it to him. Not as its king. As its light.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: We beat him three times, and the third time he broke and ran back into his fortress. Now it was our turn. We left the towers to hold the camp and sent everyone we had at his gate.

02.speaker: brannoc
02.text: Gates are my trade. Let me.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: The Pale Vesper fell on the steps of Vesperhold, still singing, and the dead she had raised lay down around her.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: In the crypt under her steps, among the dead she had not yet woken, lay my half-brother, Corvin. Six years ago he was found over a dead man, and I exiled him for murder. He had lived on the edge of the Rift ever since, watching the Gate.

03.speaker: corvin
03.text: Six years I told them it was the Marshal. Now they believe me. The man I was exiled for killing saw Cassivane cut a piece off the Heartstone. That's why he died.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: The last land was the Hollow Rift, where the war began. The Veilwalkers guard it. Their Warden, Nyxara, sleeps in the dark along its edge.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: From the edge you can see the Black Gate, miles down, and the gap in it, and a grey line of soldiers still coming out.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: Nyxara had gone mad, and the dark of the Rift climbed out over the Veilwalker towns. Their dead got up and walked, and hunters made of night walked with them. Their Herald was the Pale Vesper, the Veilwalkers' own funeral singer, who now sang the dead awake.

04.speaker: sylvaine
04.text: The dark hates growing things. Plant my forest in its road.

05.speaker: tamsin
05.text: The Veilwalkers at Lamplight say some nights a white light moves along the bottom of the Rift. Slowly. Like someone walking with a lantern.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: At Umbrael we fought the Hollow King, Nyxara's madness wearing an iron crown. When it broke, Nyxara stepped out of it with the crown in her hand.

02.speaker: nyxara
02.text: I fought it the whole time. And your Grey Lantern is alive. I hear him walking under my land, toward you.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text: All six Wardens were free, and every land was ours again.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: At Reedhaven the Saltmother's column of seawater burst on the ice. She had been the high priestess of the Tidefolk. When she fell, we found an order sewn into her robes, sending her to the Rift to study the Gate. It was sealed with Cassivane's seal.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: In the middle of the flooded reeds stood a tower of ice the sea had not broken. Inside it was Mirelle, a blind Tidefolk seer who reads the future in ice. She had kept forty children alive in there.

03.speaker: mirelle
03.text: You're late. Only a little. I saw that too.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Frostmere is a frozen sea in the north. The Tidefolk build their towns on the ice. Its Warden, Thalassa, sleeps in the water under it.

02.speaker: narrator
02.text: We fought there in the dark. Thalassa had gone mad, and the sea under the ice rose against the Tidefolk. It broke the ice from underneath, and the drowned climbed out of the holes: fishermen still casting their nets, priests still praying. They were led by the Tidefolk's own high priestess, the Saltmother.

03.speaker: tamsin
03.text:
Fennick always said water slows. Not this water. In the margin of his notes he wrote one word: fire.

So we burn it.

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Under Pearlhaven we brought down the Tidal Leviathan, an eel of grey ice as long as the harbour. It broke apart, and Thalassa rose out of the water.

02.speaker: thalassa
02.text: I remember every ship that ever sailed this sea, and every child on it. I drowned some of them this winter. I will remember that too.

03.speaker: narrator
03.text:
The sea lay down under the ice, and the holes froze over. That night Mirelle looked into the ice for a long time. She said she had seen a death at the very end of the war.

She would not say whose.
